lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: reasonableness and units

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: Which is longer: a 3-by-4 diagonal or a 5-by-12 diagonal?

steps: Identify the legs and the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle.
Use a² + b² = c² and take a square root only after finding c².

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: What does a² + b² = c² describe?
choices: the angle sum of a triangle
the side lengths of a right triangle

items.prompt: In a right triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
choices: the side next to the right angle
the side opposite the right angle

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 3 and 11. What is its hypotenuse in simplest radical form?
What is the distance between (0, 0) and (3, 9) in simplest radical form?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: Do side lengths 3, 4, and 5 satisfy the Pythagorean theorem?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Classify a triangle with side lengths 7, 24, and 25 using the converse of the Pythagorean theorem.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
